recipes.name: Bean Quesadillas
ingredients_raw: 1 (15 ounce) can black beans, rinsed and drained

steps.text: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a skillet over medium heat, and saute the onion and garlic until soft. Mix in beans, bell pepper, tomatoes, and corn; cook until heated through.
Spread 6 tortillas with equal amounts of the bean and vegetable mixture. Sprinkle with equal amounts of the Cheddar cheese, and top with the remaining tortillas to form quesadillas.
Heat 1/4 cup oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Place quesadillas in the skillet and cook, turning once, until cheese is melted and both sides are lightly browned.

raw_recipe.headline: Bean Quesadillas
raw_recipe.description: Veggies, beans, and cheese sandwiched between two tortillas then heated in oil until golden on both sides.

review.reviewBody: i thought this recipe was awesome. the only thing i did different was instead of frying them,(seemed too time consuming)i put the mixture on top of little tortillas, sprinkled it with cheese, and baked them in the oven for 10 minutes at 350. then i topped them with sour cream and guacamole. its sooooooooooo good, and the tortillas get nice and crispy. yum!

I fried these in just a smear of olive oil in a non-stick pan to reduce the fat content. Otherwise, I followed the directions given. These are really bland. I have kept the recipe and made a note to add cumin, chili flakes or powder, and oregano next time. Also, I will double the amount of cheese. To keep the filling from falling out while cooking, I recommend sprinkling most of the cheese along the outside rim to seal the two tortillas together.

What a great meal we had for dinner tonight! I followed the recipe until the very end. I tasted it and like some others have noted, it was rather bland, hence the 4 stars instead of 5 I would give for the final product. I added sea salt, cumin, and chili powder, a little at a time until I liked it. I served it with Mexican Rice I by Michele O'Sullivan (made with brown and wild rice) and guacamole by Bob Cody. Back to the quesadillas, I folded each one in half and spread a little butter on one side of the outside. I put on a big spoonful of beans and topped with shredded cheese (much more than the recipe called for). I cooked them on the electric grill until browned on each side. Topped with sour cream. Delicious! Thank you!

I used big flavored tortillas and put one down on a cookie sheet then put the sauteed ingredients on it, then sprinkled cheese on top of that and pressed another tortilla on top of all that then slid it into a preheated oven! Easy! Served with salsa, sour cream, and sliced avocado. So many things you can do with this and so many ways to make it yours.

Lovely fresh recipe. Gave me the opportunity to use up stuff in my garden. I try to never change recipes prior to a first make but this one required a few just based on experience. I put salsa verde in the mixture while it was simmering. I did this because people mentioned the challenge of flipping the quesadilla (ingredients falling out on flip). It makes the mixture stick together and it gives it some seasoning. You could also use a little water and taco seasoning or regular salsa (as long as it's more liquid than chunky). I think people are afraid salsa verde will turn their food green and it does not...anyhoo, the only other feedback I have is that there was no seasoning. I added a bit of salt and pepper, a small jalapeño (had it in the garden - otherwise wouldn't have) and of course the salsa verde. The key to quesadillas when flipping is be patient. I use low heat, let it sit, check regularly. Good luck!

This was great! I found the veggie mixture a little bland, so added 1 tbsp chili powder and 1 tsp ground cumin. I covered half of the tortillas with filling, topped with cheese and cilantro, then folded them in half and broiled them for a few minutes per side, without olive oil. I served them with sour cream, guacamole and salsa. They received rave reviews from adults and kids alike! An easy, tasty, satisfying and nutritious vegetarian weeknight meal. Thanks for a keeper!

I like it, but I had to make some changes. I added cilantro, cumin, chili powder, and lime juice. I don't know why people have a hard time flipping these over. I just put some cheese down first then the veggies and more cheese. When the cheese melts at the bottom the veggies stick to it. Hardly anything comes out. I also put the tomatoes on a paper towel to get rid of the juice. It reminds me of the black bean burritos I make.

Overall very good! Few modifications: did not use fresh garlic, 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tsp each: Mexican Tajin seasoning, chili powder and cumin. Dash of salt and pepper. 1/2 green pepper and red pepper. After everything was heated, added 1/4 cup chopped cilantro and 1/2 of a small zucchini shredded. 3 cups of cheese ( half cheddar and half jalepeno Monterey jack). Unless used 10 tortillas, delish!!!

I baked these, which was easier and healthier than frying them. Due to a tomato snafu, I replaced the tomato with spinach and tomato paste (long story). They turned out well, if a little messy! I added some spices (chili powder and red pepper) too.

Why would you use 1/4 c oil for frying in this recipe? It's under "healthy dinners", and besides the oil is completely unnecessary.... A great basic idea, and hey I used it, but not really any kind of healthy with the oil, full fat cheese, and flour tortillas. If you slightly mash your beans (to help the two sides stick together), and add something spicy (jalapenos, even cilantro would work), then just fill and cook them in a dry pan (doesn't even have to be non-stick-- just wait for them to get nice and brown before trying to move them and they'll slide around neatly with minimal coaxing), you'll have a much healthier version. Also try it with corn tortillas if you can, they're better for you (less fat including saturated, less calories, less additives/ingredients).

I did add salt, cumin and my own fajita seasoning mix I make, it was so very good. BUT everything came flying out trying to flip them so I started just putting the goodies on half, and folding them on the skillet and then flipping with the folded side down and that worked much better!
I added a little adobo spice and some of the salsa I prefer
I want to add some seasonings next time, but otherwise very fresh and simple meal.
I am the only one who like black beans in my family but everyone loved these!

The recipe is very filling for the quesadillas. However, the next time, I would just use one tortilla and fold it over instead of trying to put two together. The filling tends to fall out in that case which is no bueno! Much better with a folded quesadilla.
Nice with salmon Muenster Cheese and pico de gallo buttered and grilled.
The entire family enjoyed this recipe. I also added hamburger and shredded cheese. Leftovers we used tortilla chips and made nachos.
Delicious and easy, no need to place quesadillas in skillet, stick 'em right in the oven!

The filling was very good but there was too much of it. Besides that my family enjoyed it tho it was difficult to flip in the pan. next time i make it I will probably just make the filling and add meat.

We enjoyed these very much! I added chicken, and it was very good. I think I might try the baking method as another reviewer suggested. When I flip them some filling falls out and the cheese burns in the pan. Oops. Still delicious though. A great, easy meal for any day!
